2.01.b:
### One road for every patient
- Handbook algorithm → **plain X-ray → MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) of the whole bone → bone scan → metastatic work-up if malignant → biopsy last** (Handbook)
- Prof Abosena → history → examination → labs → X-ray → MRI → CT, scan or PET → **biopsy**; the final answer = the **stage** (Prof Abosena)

### History and examination — the work-up starts here
- Pain → duration, onset, **night, rest or mechanical** · red flags → wakes the patient, prevents sleep, worsens quickly, no relation to effort (Prof Abosena)
- Ask the past history twice ("simple gland operation" = removed cancer) · general examination **3–4 minutes** → thyroid, nodes, breasts, abdomen, prostate (Prof Abosena)

CLINICAL PEARL — one minute of examination
- Mammography, bone scan, core and open biopsy → no diagnosis
- A breast mass discharging for 3 years → one look would have found it (Prof Abosena)

2.02.b:
### Plain X-ray — always first
- X-ray first, **not MRI first** → the map of the lesion → 1 Reading the Film · two planes of the **whole host bone**
- Many benign lesions are diagnosed by the film alone → osteochondroma, non-ossifying fibroma, enchondroma, simple bone cyst
- Normal film until **30–50% of the bone** is destroyed → normal film + symptoms = MRI (Prof Abosena)

- Proximal humerus, permeative lesion with fracture, 64-year-old: high-grade osteosarcoma (OKU Tumors 4)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | central | osteolytic | ill-defined (permeative) | destruction | pathological fracture | **malignant** |

CLINICAL PEARL — the old patient is not always a metastasis
- A lytic lesion at 64 may be a **primary sarcoma** → finish the work-up and biopsy **before** fixing the fracture (Campbell)

### MRI — the rules
- **With contrast**; T1, T2, STIR (short tau inversion recovery) · **whole bone**, joint to joint → finds the **skip lesion** (Prof Abosena)
- Shows → extent, soft-tissue mass, skip lesion, **relation to vessels and nerves**
- Aggressive → ill-defined, cortical breakthrough, enhancing mass · non-aggressive → well-defined, especially a **dark rim** (Campbell)
- Specific only for lipoma, haemangioma, haematoma, PVNS (pigmented villonodular synovitis) · soft-tissue mass **deep or >5 cm** → sarcoma until proved otherwise (Campbell)

CLINICAL PEARL — margins belong to the film
- Zone of transition → read on **X-ray or CT**, not MRI; MRI can **overestimate** a non-aggressive lesion (OKU Tumors 4)

PITFALL — "always with contrast"
- Prof Abosena → always · OKU → not needed in every case
- Say → "**MRI with contrast** for a suspected tumour; contrast shows the viable part to biopsy"

- Osteosarcoma, distal femur, 13-year-old: films, MRI, PET with skip lesions (OKU Tumors 4)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | central | mixed | ill-defined | destruction + periosteal reaction | skip lesion | **malignant** |

- Osteosarcoma, distal femur, 11-year-old: skip lesion on STIR MRI (Salom 2021, open access)

### Bone scan — principles and the three phases
- **Technetium-99m methylene diphosphonate** → mineral turnover (blood flow + osteoblasts) → counts **all skeletal lesions** in one study (Handbook)

| Phase | Time | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Flow | Seconds | Blood flow |
| 2 Blood pool | Minutes | Congestion → inflammation or infection |
| 3 Delayed | Hours | Isotope bound to **osteoblasts** → new bone formation |

- **Sensitive, not specific** → benign and malignant lesions both hot · not routine → suspected sarcoma or metastasis (Prof Abosena)
- Uses → multiple lesions, small lesions such as osteoid osteoma (nidus → **double-density sign**)

- Breast carcinoma metastases: hot skull, spine and pelvis on bone scan (Greenspan)
- Bone scan slide: leg and knee films, scans, breast MRI; diagnosis not stated by the lecturer; strip = knee film (Prof Abosena)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | eccentric | osteosclerotic | well-defined | intact | none | **benign latent** |

- Osteoid osteoma, proximal tibia: bone scan and SPECT/CT (Parmeggiani 2021, open access)

### Multiple lesions — risk and syndrome
- Group members → 1 Differential · this table adds **single or multiple, the syndrome, the risk** (Handbook)

| Condition | Usually | Multiple form · syndrome | Risk / key fact |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metastasis, myeloma, lymphoma, leukaemia | Multiple | — | **Commonest cause of multiple lesions in adults** |
| Osteochondroma | Single | Multiple hereditary exostoses | Chondrosarcoma ≈1% single, **≈5% in MHE (multiple hereditary exostoses)** (Campbell) |
| Enchondroma | Single | Ollier · Maffucci (+ haemangiomas) | Ollier ≈25% malignancy by 40; Maffucci higher (Campbell) |
| Fibrous dysplasia | Monostotic | McCune-Albright → polyostotic + pigmentation + precocious puberty | Higher risk with the syndrome |
| Non-ossifying fibroma | Single | Jaffe-Campanacci → multiple NOF (non-ossifying fibroma) + café-au-lait | Benign; resolves |
| Tumour-like | — | Brown tumour · bone infarct · Brodie's abscess | Find the metabolic or infective cause |

### Cold lesions — real question
- Real question (Nagah p31) → "Which bone tumours are **cold** on bone scan?" · **cold** = no uptake → **purely lytic**, no osteoblastic reaction (Handbook)

| Cold lesion | Why |
|---|---|
| **Multiple myeloma** (commonest) | Purely lytic, no reactive new bone (Greenspan) |
| **Renal cell carcinoma** (some) | Lytic metastasis (Campbell) |
| Thyroid, breast, melanoma metastases · lymphoma | Lytic (Handbook) |
| Histiocytosis (eosinophilic granuloma) | Scan may be falsely negative (Campbell) |
| Chordoma | Cold centre |
| Bone island (benign) | Normal uptake → excludes osteoid osteoma (Greenspan) |

- Next step → **skeletal survey** (one view of each limb, AP (anteroposterior) pelvis, whole spine, lateral skull) (Handbook); in myeloma more sensitive than the scan (Miller)
- PET shows the lytic disease the scan misses · cold myeloma on film → 11 Multiple myeloma · 6

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "cold lesions"
- Say → "A cold lesion has no osteoblastic reaction. The classic one is **multiple myeloma**; also some **renal cell** metastases and other purely lytic deposits."
- Then → "In histiocytosis and chordoma the scan may also be falsely negative. So I would ask for a **skeletal survey**, or whole-body MRI or PET."

- Bone island of the scaphoid: film and normal bone scan (Greenspan)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| scaphoid | — | osteosclerotic | well-defined | intact | none | **benign latent** |

- Multiple myeloma: skull lytic lesions and FDG PET, PET/CT (Greenspan)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| skull | — | osteolytic | well-defined (no rim) | destruction | multiple | **malignant** |

- Multiple myeloma of the humerus with an old pathological fracture (Healy 2011, open access)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | ill-defined (moth-eaten) | thinning | multiple · pathological fracture | **malignant** |

### Metastatic work-up
- After malignancy is suspected → find the metastases and the **primary** · CT chest, abdomen, pelvis; mammogram, thyroid scan by suspicion (Handbook)

| Item | Campbell protocol — older than 40, new painful lesion, no known primary |
|---|---|
| Likely | Myeloma or metastatic carcinoma |
| Primary | Known cancer → prostate, breast · unknown → **lung, kidney** |
| Examine | Thyroid, lungs, abdomen, prostate, breasts |
| Labs | CBC (complete blood count), ESR (erythrocyte sedimentation rate), electrolytes, liver enzymes, alkaline phosphatase, SPEP (serum protein electrophoresis), PSA (prostate-specific antigen) |
| Imaging | X-ray of the bone and chest · bone scan · CT chest, abdomen, pelvis |
| Result | Primary found in **85%** (Campbell) |

- Primary sarcoma → MRI of the whole bone, bone scan, CT chest or whole-body PET-CT

- Humeral fracture, 81-year-old: bone scan and CT find a renal carcinoma (Campbell)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | ill-defined (permeative) | destruction | pathological fracture | **malignant** |

- Thyroid carcinoma: iodine-131 whole-body scan and spine MRI (Greenspan)

### CT — computed tomography
- **Cortex and matrix** → nidus, thin ABC (aneurysmal bone cyst) rim, cartilage calcification, endosteal erosion · **investigation of choice in osteoid osteoma** (Prof Abosena)
- **CT chest** → best for lung metastases · CT with contrast when MRI is impossible (Campbell)

- CT slide: lung metastases; osteoid osteoma of the tibia (lecture context) (Prof Abosena)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diaphyseal | cortical | osteosclerotic | well-defined | intact | nidus on CT | **benign active** |

- Chondrosarcoma, proximal femur, 70-year-old: film and axial CT (Greenspan)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diaphyseal | central | mixed | ill-defined | destruction + soft-tissue mass | fluffy cotton calcification | **malignant** |

- Chondrosarcoma of the scapula: axial CT (Greenspan)

### PET — positron emission tomography
- **FDG** (fluorodeoxyglucose) trapped in high-metabolism tissue → bone scan uses a radionuclide, PET a **metabolite** (Prof Abosena) · **SUV** (standardized uptake value) rises with chondrosarcoma grade
- Uses → whole-body staging (occult metastases, nodes) · biopsy target · chemotherapy response · recurrence, unknown primary
- Bone metastases in the young → FDG PET **90%** vs whole-body MRI 82% vs bone scan 71% (Greenspan)
- Limits → false positive in inflammation; misses small lung metastases → CT chest still needed (Campbell)

- Lung carcinoma metastases: whole-body PET and fused PET/CT (Greenspan)
- Ewing sarcoma, proximal fibula, 23-year-old: PET/CT (Greenspan)

2.03.b:
### Routine panel
- Labs **rarely make the diagnosis** · **no tumour markers in sarcoma** (osteosarcoma, Ewing) (Prof Abosena)
- Routine → CBC, ESR, CRP (C-reactive protein), calcium, renal and liver function (Handbook)

| Test | Raised in |
|---|---|
| ESR | Infection · metastatic carcinoma · small round-cell tumours |
| Calcium | Metastasis · myeloma · hyperparathyroidism |
| Alkaline phosphatase | Metabolic bone disease · metastasis · osteosarcoma · Ewing · lymphoma |
| Albumin <3.5 g/dL or lymphocytes <1500/mL | Wound problems and infection (Campbell) |

### Specific tests by suspicion
| Suspicion | Test |
|---|---|
| Metabolic · brown tumour | Vitamin D · PTH (parathormone) + calcium |
| Paget disease | Alkaline phosphatase · urinary pyridinium cross-links (Campbell) |
| Prostate · ovary · colon · liver | PSA, acid phosphatase · CA125 · CEA (carcinoembryonic antigen) · AFP (alpha-fetoprotein) |
| Myeloma, leukaemia, lymphoma | Serum and urine electrophoresis · Bence Jones · M protein · marrow aspirate |

- Myeloma → skeletal survey + marrow biopsy; proved by labs → **no bone biopsy needed** (Campbell)

2.04.b:
### Types of biopsy
| Type | Tissue | Use in bone |
|---|---|---|
| Cytology · FNA (fine-needle aspiration) | Cells only, no architecture | Not for primary bone tumours; recurrence, metastatic carcinoma |
| **Core needle** (CT- or ultrasound-guided) | Cells + stroma | First choice; several samples; accuracy **>90%** (OKU Tumors 4) |
| **Open incisional** | Adequate block | Gold standard; more complications; after a failed core |
| Excisional | Whole lesion | Small lesion, expendable bone, typical film (osteochondroma) |
| Frozen section | Rapid | Confirms diagnostic tissue; lower quality |

- Bone needs **cells + stroma** → core, not cytology · core may miss (reactive zone, necrosis) · immunohistochemistry names the spindle-cell sarcoma (Prof Abosena)

- Coaxial core needle biopsy system (OKU Tumors 4)
- Presacral schwannoma: MRI and CT-guided core biopsy (OKU Tumors 4)
- Destroyed L4 pedicle, 67-year-old: percutaneous biopsy, colon metastasis (Greenspan)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| posterior elements | — | osteolytic | ill-defined | destruction | absent pedicle | **malignant** |

### Surgical principles of open biopsy
| Rule | What to do |
|---|---|
| Incision | **Longitudinal**, in line with the definitive incision; never transverse (wider resection and radiotherapy field) |
| Dissection | **Through one muscle**, shortest route; no new compartments; away from the neurovascular bundle |
| Sampling | **Soft-tissue extension** or periphery; avoid the necrotic centre |
| Bone window | Only if no soft-tissue mass; **oblong with rounded ends** → width weakens, length does not (Operative Techniques) |
| Hole · tourniquet | Plug with methacrylate · elevate, **never exsanguinate**; deflate before closure |
| Drain · closure | Exits **in line with the incision**, at its end · tight, in layers |
| Specimen | Frozen section for adequacy · culture what you biopsy |

- Immediate definitive surgery → new drapes and instruments · tracts → **transdeltoid** for the proximal humerus

- Biopsy tracts by site: humerus, femur, tibia, drawings (Operative Techniques)
- Longitudinal vs transverse biopsy incisions, drawings and cases (Operative Techniques)
- Cortical window shapes; fracture after a large window (Operative Techniques)
- Round biopsy hole in bone, operative photo (Campbell)

PITFALL — the Handbook's closure and sampling lines
- Handbook → leave muscle open, sample capsule + reactive zone + normal tissue · Campbell → close in layers, contaminate little
- Say → "Sample the soft-tissue edge of the tumour and close tightly in layers"

- Drain site in line with the incision; a misplaced flank drain (Operative Techniques)

### Biopsy is the last step
- **Last step, not the first** (Handbook) · "no cancer operation without a cancer diagnosis" (OKU Tumors 4) · planned **as carefully as the definitive operation**
- Why it waits (Rougraff) → may be a primary sarcoma (track for limb salvage) · easier lesion found · **renal carcinoma → embolise first**
- Myeloma proved by labs · imaging guides the pathologist · frozen section of a proven "metastasis" → fix the same sitting (Campbell)

### The badly placed biopsy
- Poorly performed biopsies, seven errors (Campbell)
- A biopsy that forces plastic cover or amputation → **malpractice** (OKU Tumors 4) · errors more frequent at a **referring hospital** (Campbell)

### Who does it and track excision
- The surgeon of the **definitive operation** or the oncology centre · suspected sarcoma → **refer before biopsy**; metastasis or myeloma → local core reasonable
- **Biopsy track contaminated** → excised en bloc · contaminated in **32% of open** vs 0.8% of percutaneous biopsies (OKU Tumors 4)

- Biopsy scar and track excised with a distal femoral osteosarcoma (Operative Techniques)
- Viable melanoma in a resected biopsy track, histology (Operative Techniques)

PITFALL — must every needle track be excised?
- Campbell → every track · OKU → needle tracks controversial
- Say → "Plan every track inside the definitive incision; **excise open-biopsy tracks**, needle tracks by the surgeon's decision"

| Dissection | **Through one muscle**, shortest route; no new compartments; away from the neurovascular bundle |
| Sampling | **Soft-tissue extension** or periphery; avoid the necrotic centre |
| Bone window | Only if no soft-tissue mass; **oblong with rounded ends** → width weakens, length does not (Operative Techniques) |
| Hole · tourniquet | Plug with methacrylate · elevate, **never exsanguinate**; deflate before closure |
| Drain · closure | Exits **in line with the incision**, at its end · tight, in layers |
| Specimen | Frozen section for adequacy · culture what you biopsy |

- Immediate definitive surgery → new drapes and instruments · tracts → **transdeltoid** for the proximal humerus

- Biopsy tracts by site: humerus, femur, tibia, drawings (Operative Techniques)
- Longitudinal vs transverse biopsy incisions, drawings and cases (Operative Techniques)
- Cortical window shapes; fracture after a large window (Operative Techniques)
- Round biopsy hole in bone, operative photo (Campbell)

PITFALL — the Handbook's closure and sampling lines
- Handbook → leave muscle open, sample capsule + reactive zone + normal tissue · Campbell → close in layers, contaminate little
- Say → "Sample the soft-tissue edge of the tumour and close tightly in layers"

- Drain site in line with the incision; a misplaced flank drain (Operative Techniques)

2.04.3.b:
- **Last step, not the first** (Handbook) · "no cancer operation without a cancer diagnosis" (OKU Tumors 4) · planned **as carefully as the definitive operation**
- Why it waits (Rougraff) → may be a primary sarcoma (track for limb salvage) · easier lesion found · **renal carcinoma → embolise first**
- Myeloma proved by labs · imaging guides the pathologist · frozen section of a proven "metastasis" → fix the same sitting (Campbell)

2.04.4.b:
- Poorly performed biopsies, seven errors (Campbell)
- A biopsy that forces plastic cover or amputation → **malpractice** (OKU Tumors 4) · errors more frequent at a **referring hospital** (Campbell)

2.04.5.t: Who does it and track excision
2.04.5.b:
- The surgeon of the **definitive operation** or the oncology centre · suspected sarcoma → **refer before biopsy**; metastasis or myeloma → local core reasonable
- **Biopsy track contaminated** → excised en bloc · contaminated in **32% of open** vs 0.8% of percutaneous biopsies (OKU Tumors 4)

- Biopsy scar and track excised with a distal femoral osteosarcoma (Operative Techniques)
- Viable melanoma in a resected biopsy track, histology (Operative Techniques)

PITFALL — must every needle track be excised?
- Campbell → every track · OKU → needle tracks controversial
- Say → "Plan every track inside the definitive incision; **excise open-biopsy tracks**, needle tracks by the surgeon's decision"

2.05.b:
### Malignant features
- Gross → haemorrhage, necrosis, soft-tissue invasion · microscopy → **hypercellularity, high mitotic rate**, scanty matrix, pleomorphism, atypia (Handbook)
- Grade (three grades) → the strongest predictor of **metastasis**; most malignant bone tumours are high grade (Miller)
- Diagnosis → H&E (haematoxylin and eosin) section, then **immunohistochemistry** for the subtype (Prof Abosena)

### The Handbook's differential method
- Always → **by location → by cortex (expansile or not) → by cell → the mimic** (Handbook); lists → 1 Differential
- **Stellate cells** → giant cell tumour, chondromyxoid fibroma · specific groups → brown tumour, Paget, infection, bone infarct (Handbook)

| Step (giant cell tumour example) | Profile | Rule out |
|---|---|---|
| By location | **Epiphyseal** | Chondroblastoma, clear cell chondrosarcoma, Brodie's abscess, subchondral cyst |
| By cortex | **Expansile** | Cysts, benign cartilage tumours, osteoblastoma, NOF, fibrous dysplasia |
| By cell | **Giant cells** | ABC, brown tumour, chondroblastoma, NOF, osteoblastoma |
| Mimic | Benign, **non-mimicking** | — (→ 5 GCT · 9) |

2.06.b:
### Benign tumours — latent, active, aggressive
| Stage | Behaviour · film | Examples · treatment (Handbook) |
|---|---|---|
| **1 Latent** | Stops at maturity, intracapsular · well-defined, thick rim | Simple bone cyst, osteoid osteoma, osteochondroma, enchondroma, NOF, fibrous dysplasia → observation, steroid, simple curettage |
| **2 Active** | Grows past maturity · thin rim, may expand the cortex | Cellular enchondroma, active fibrous dysplasia → curettage |
| **3 Aggressive** | Unlimited, breaks barriers · broken rim, soft-tissue mass | ABC, giant cell tumour, chondromyxoid fibroma, "-blastoma" → curettage + adjuvant or en bloc |

- Chondroblastoma, chondromyxoid fibroma → usually stage 2, rarely 3 (Campbell) → 6 · stage 3 → lung metastasis in **1–5%** (GCT) though benign (Campbell)
- Latent = "leave it alone and it leaves you alone" (Prof Abosena) · the same three words are the Frame A **verdict** → 1 Verdict

- Benign staging slide: B simple bone cyst, C giant cell tumour (lecture context); A unnamed (Prof Abosena)

| Film | Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A distal femur | metaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined | intact | none | **benign latent** |
| B humerus | metaphyseal + diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined | thinning + expansion | none | **benign active** |
| C knee + MRI | epiphyseal + metaphyseal | eccentric | osteolytic | ill-defined | destruction | none | **benign aggressive** |

PITFALL — simple bone cyst: latent or active?
- Handbook → latent · Campbell → active **within 1 cm of the physis**
- Say → "Grade the cyst you see: near the physis active, away from it latent" → 4 Cysts

### Malignant tumours — Enneking (MSTS system)
- **Grade, compartment, metastasis** (Campbell) · compartment → bounded by cortex, articular cartilage, fascial septa, capsule

| Stage | Grade | Site | Metastasis |
|---|---|---|---|
| **IA** | Low (G1) | Intracompartmental (T1) | None |
| **IB** | Low (G1) | Extracompartmental (T2) | None |
| **IIA** | High (G2) | Intracompartmental (T1) | None |
| **IIB** | High (G2) | Extracompartmental (T2) | None |
| **III** | Any | Any | **Regional or distant** (M1) |

- Low grade → metastatic risk **<25%** · stage III → nodes and distant not separated · benign stages Arabic (1–3), malignant Roman (I–III) (Campbell)

- Enneking stage IA: low-grade chondrosarcoma, proximal femur (Campbell)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | central | mixed | ill-defined | thinning | none | **malignant** |

- Enneking stage IIB: osteosarcoma, proximal humerus (Campbell)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | central | mixed | ill-defined | destruction + soft-tissue mass | tumour bone | **malignant** |

EXAM PEARL — Enneking in one line
- "**Roman number = grade** (I low, II high) · **letter = compartment** (A inside, B outside) · **III = any metastasis**" (memory aid)

### Malignant tumours — AJCC (American Joint Committee on Cancer), bone
- **Size, grade, nodes, metastasis** → T1 ≤8 cm · T2 >8 cm · T3 **skip lesion in the same bone** · G1 low, G2–G3 high (OKU Tumors 4)
- AJCC = the universal system; Enneking = the orthopaedic historical one

| Stage | T | N | M | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **IA** | T1 (≤8 cm) | N0 | M0 | Low |
| **IB** | T2 (>8 cm) or T3 | N0 | M0 | Low |
| **IIA** | T1 | N0 | M0 | High |
| **IIB** | T2 | N0 | M0 | High |
| **III** | T3 (skip) | N0 | M0 | High |
| **IVA** | Any | N0 | **M1a — lung** | Any |
| **IVB** | Any | **N1** or any | Any or **M1b — other distant sites** | Any |

- Non-lung metastases do **worse** than lung-only · nodes rare, but **any node = IVB** · soft-tissue sarcoma → own system, cut-off **5 cm** → 12 Soft-tissue sarcoma

PITFALL — the Handbook's AJCC stage 4
- Handbook → 4A node, 4B distant, grades G1–G4 · OKU, Campbell → **IVA lung, IVB node or other site**, G1–G3
- Say → "Stage IV is metastasis: **IVA lung, IVB nodes or bone and other organs**"

### Why stage
- **Prognosis** and **treatment plan**; also results and communication · prognostic factors → **grade**, extent, **size >8 cm**, metastasis (Prof Abosena)

- Prognostic slide: humerus film, MRI, lung CT; likely osteosarcoma on the film (our reading; not stated by the lecturer) (Prof Abosena)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | central | osteosclerotic | ill-defined | destruction + soft-tissue mass | lung nodules on CT | **malignant** |

### Worked examples — stage the patient
| Patient | Enneking | AJCC |
|---|---|---|
| Low-grade chondrosarcoma, inside the femur, 6 cm, no metastasis | **IA** | **IA** |
| High-grade osteosarcoma, through the cortex into muscle, 10 cm, no metastasis | **IIB** | **IIB** |
| High-grade osteosarcoma with a skip lesion in the same femur, no other spread | — | **III** |
| Any osteosarcoma with lung metastases only | **III** | **IVA** |
| Any sarcoma with a regional lymph node | **III** | **IVB** |

- Prof Abosena → T1 M0 G1 = **IA**; T1 M1 G1 = **III** (Prof Abosena)

CLINICAL PEARL — answer "which stage" in one breath
- Benign → **latent, active or aggressive** · malignant → **grade, compartment or size, metastasis** → name both: "Enneking IIB, AJCC IIB" (Prof Abosena)

EXAM PEARL — The examiner asks
- **Cold lesions on bone scan?** → myeloma; some renal metastases; histiocytosis; chordoma → skeletal survey
- **Rules of open biopsy?** → longitudinal, through one muscle, no new compartments, tight closure, drain in line
- **Why is biopsy last?** → plan a track for limb salvage; easier lesion; embolise renal; myeloma by labs
- **Enneking vs AJCC?** → Enneking grade/compartment/metastasis; AJCC size 8 cm/grade/skip/node/lung vs other
